backlog.spec: Inside the restart loop, right after a restart finishes and is repaired, check whether its sum is within 0.004 of the current best sum (or is the new best). If so, rerun SLSQP once from that restart's raw solution, with normal(0, 0.003) noise added to the centres, radii multiplied by 0.98, and maxiter 100; repair the result and keep it if it is better. Do this at most once per restart, with no pool and no separate phase: the main loop stays pure random restarts until TIME_FRACTION. This differs from the best-only polish of slot 39 and the pool methods of slots 9 and 22, because every near-best basin gets one cheap escape attempt from a saddle or a premature stop, at the moment it is found.
backlog.title: Second tap on near-best restarts

backlog.spec: In each restart, run SLSQP first with the radii fixed to a common value equal to 0.9 times the largest feasible equal radius, done by optimising only the centres to maximise the minimum pair gap for 40 iterations. Then run the full SLSQP on centres and radii from that point. This gives a feasible, spread-out start.
backlog.title: Two-phase radius target SLSQP

backlog.spec: Each restart first solves a packing for n-k circles (k = 2 or 3, chosen at random) with the same SLSQP call. Then it inserts the k new circles at the centres of the largest empty holes found by a 60x60 grid search of max(min distance to centres, distance to walls). Their initial radii are the hole clearance times 0.9. It then runs SLSQP on all n circles and repairs as before. Keep the time-limit loop unchanged.
backlog.title: Incremental growth from a smaller packing

backlog.spec: After the restarts, take the best packing. Do 10 rounds of: (1) solve a scipy linprog for the radii at the fixed centres, maximising the sum of radii under the pair and wall constraints; (2) run SLSQP for 30 iterations from the result. Keep the result if the repaired sum improves.
backlog.title: Alternating LP radii and centre polish

backlog.spec: Replace the SLSQP call in _solve_once with an augmented Lagrangian loop. Variables are the centres and radii with box bounds (centres in [0, 1], radii in [0, 0.3]), handled by L-BFGS-B. The constraints are g = pair gaps d_ij - r_i - r_j and wall gaps. Minimise -sum(r) + sum over constraints of (mu/2)*max(0, lam/mu - g)^2, with a vectorised analytic gradient. Do 8 outer rounds of 200 L-BFGS-B iterations each. After each round update lam = max(0, lam - mu*g) and multiply mu by 3, starting from mu = 10. Keep the existing repair step. The aim is much cheaper restarts than O(n^2)-constraint SLSQP, so many more of them.
backlog.title: Augmented Lagrangian with L-BFGS-B instead of SLSQP

backlog.spec: Change the pair constraints to (dx^2+dy^2) - (ri+rj)^2 >= 0, which is smooth at zero distance. Add the analytic Jacobian for these. Keep the wall constraints linear. Also add the constraint ri+rj >= 0 implicitly through r >= 0, which is already present. The repair step stays as is.
backlog.title: Squared-distance constraints with Jacobian

backlog.spec: Make the SLSQP iteration cap grow across restarts. Restart k uses maxiter = min(200, 40 * 2**(k // 4)), so early restarts are cheap and later ones run to convergence. Keep the same hex init, repair and best-tracking. Pass the cap into _solve_once as an argument instead of reading the MAX_ITER constant.
backlog.title: Iterated-deepening SLSQP budget

backlog.spec: Apply both changes that individually scored -2.9396 (slots 6 and 19; each a single run within noise of the incumbent) in one edit. (a) Give SLSQP an analytic objective gradient (zeros for centres, -1 for radii) and a dense analytic constraint Jacobian for the pair-distance and wall constraints, guarding the distance division with max(d, 1e-12). (b) Before SLSQP, relax the jittered hex-grid centres with 30 L-BFGS-B iterations on the squared-overlap penalty sum(max(0, 2*INIT_RADIUS - d_ij)^2) plus the matching wall penalty, with analytic gradient and bounds [INIT_RADIUS, 1-INIT_RADIUS]. Keep MAX_ITER, TIME_FRACTION and the repair unchanged. The aim is to test whether the two unconfirmed gains add up to something above the 0.0034 noise sd.
backlog.title: Combine analytic Jacobian with L-BFGS-B centre pre-relaxation

backlog.spec: For each row of the hex init, add an independent random horizontal phase in [0,1/(m+0.5)) with wrap-around, and choose the stagger amplitude randomly in {0.3,0.5,0.7}. Keep jitter 0.02, 5 to 7 rows and the random subset. This diversifies the lattice defects.
backlog.title: Larger row-offset hex init with random column phase

backlog.spec: Before each SLSQP run, generate a batch of 6 candidate inits with the current hex-grid recipe (independent row count, subset and jitter) and score each without optimisation: set r_i = min(wall distance, half the distance to the nearest neighbour), which is always feasible, and use sum(r_i) as the score. Run SLSQP only from one candidate, sampled with probability proportional to exp((score - max score)/0.02), so that the choice is biased towards well-spread inits but is not greedy. Start SLSQP with the constant INIT_RADIUS as now, not the scored radii. Keep the repair and the restart loop unchanged. The scoring is a few vectorised numpy lines and costs far less than one SLSQP iteration.
backlog.title: Pick the best of a batch of inits by a cheap score

backlog.spec: Replace the independent normal jitter (sd 0.02) on the hex-grid points with a smooth random deformation that keeps the local hexagonal order. Draw 4 random low-frequency modes per restart: displacement(x, y) = sum_k a_k * sin(pi*(p_k*x + q_k*y) + phi_k), with p_k, q_k integers in {0,1,2} (not both zero), phase phi_k uniform in [0, 2*pi), and vector amplitudes a_k drawn from normal(0, 0.015) per coordinate. Add this displacement to the grid points, plus a small iid jitter of sd 0.005 to break ties, then clip to [0.03, 0.97] as now. Leave the row-count draw, the random subset, SLSQP and the repair unchanged.
backlog.title: Smooth warp of the hex grid instead of iid jitter

backlog.spec: Replace the iterative pairwise shrink in _repair with one global scale. Compute the factor s = min over all pairs of d_ij / (r_i + r_j) and over all walls of the wall clearance divided by r_i, with s capped at 1. Multiply all radii by s, then subtract SHRINK and clamp at zero. This is cheap, one vectorised pass, and always gives a valid packing. Keep the rest of solve unchanged.
backlog.title: Global-scale feasibility repair

backlog.spec: In _solve_once, place about 4*sqrt(n) of the circles first on the four edges of the square at random positions with radius 0.05. Place the remaining circles uniformly at random in the interior [0.1, 0.9]^2. Add N(0, 0.01) jitter and clip to [0.03, 0.97]. Keep the initial radius as INIT_RADIUS and run the usual SLSQP and repair. The edge seeding gives boundary-hugging circles, which optimal packings often have.
backlog.title: Two-sided boundary-first init

backlog.spec: In _solve_once, after building the staggered hex points, apply an independent random affine stretch about the centre (0.5, 0.5): scale x by sx ~ U(0.85, 1.0) and y by sy ~ U(0.85, 1.0), then add the usual jitter and clip to [0.03, 0.97]. This varies the aspect ratio of the lattice, so that the row and column spacings fit the square in different ways. Everything else stays the same.
backlog.title: Anisotropic stretch of the hex grid

backlog.spec: In the init, pick 3 to 6 random points of the hex grid and give them initial radius 0.10 to 0.12. Give the others radius 0.05 and drop the nearest neighbours of the large points. Jitter and run SLSQP as before. Known good packings for this problem have a mix of radii.
backlog.title: Mixed-size hex init with a few big circles

backlog.spec: Split each restart in two SLSQP stages. Stage 1 solves the congruent-circle problem from the jittered hex-grid centres: variables are the 2n centre coordinates and one shared radius t, the objective is -t, and the constraints are d_ij - 2t >= 0 and the four wall constraints with t; cap it at 60 iterations. Stage 2 is the existing SLSQP on centres and individual radii, started from the stage-1 centres with all radii equal to t, with maxiter MAX_ITER. Keep the repair and the restart loop unchanged. The aim is to start the full problem from a jammed, well-spread configuration instead of small non-touching circles.
backlog.title: Equal-radius warm start then release

backlog.spec: Run each restart in two SLSQP stages with the same constraints. Stage 1 (40 iterations) maximises sum(r**p) with p drawn per restart from {0.5, 2.0}: p = 0.5 favours equal circles, p = 2.0 favours a few large circles with small ones filling the gaps. For p = 0.5 use sum(sqrt(r + 1e-6)) to keep the gradient finite at zero. Stage 2 starts from the stage-1 result and maximises sum(r) with maxiter MAX_ITER, as now. One restart in three skips stage 1, so the current behaviour stays in the mix. Keep the init, the repair and the restart loop unchanged. The aim is to reach size distributions that the plain objective does not reach from equal initial radii.
backlog.title: Area-objective homotopy before the radius-sum objective

backlog.spec: Define three start families: the existing jittered hex grid, the square lattice with deletions, and the greedy maximal-hole init. Track each family's best repaired radius sum and its number of runs. For each restart after the first 6, pick the family with the highest upper confidence bound, mean best plus 0.02*sqrt(log(total)/count), with ties broken by rng. Use the same SLSQP and repair for every family, and keep the time-limit loop as is.
backlog.title: Family bandit over init types

backlog.spec: Add an analytic objective gradient (-1 for radius entries, 0 for centres) and a dense analytic constraint Jacobian for the pair, wall and radius constraints. Pass them to SLSQP via jac=. Raise MAX_ITER to 300 so that each run converges more fully. Keep the hex init and the repair unchanged.
backlog.title: Analytic gradient and Jacobian with MAX_ITER 300

backlog.spec: In _solve_once, first solve a reduced problem with all radii tied to one variable t, maximising t subject to the same pair and wall constraints, using SLSQP from the jittered hex start. Use the resulting centres and t as the start for the usual free-radius SLSQP, with each radius initialised to t. This gives the free problem a feasible, evenly spread start. Keep MAX_ITER and the repair step unchanged.
backlog.title: Equal-radius start before free SLSQP

memo:
Helped: only the init change in slot 0 (jittered staggered hex grid, 5-7 rows, random subset of positions): -2.9253 to -2.9375 (delta -0.0123), well above noise sd 0.0034. It is a single run, not yet replicated. Slots 6, 19 and 33 (-2.9396, delta -0.0020) are within noise, so they are possible but unconfirmed. Slot 31 (-0.0005) is noise.
Did not help: schedule edits (2-4, 7, 13, 23-25), bounds (1), analytic gradients alone (5), trust-constr polish (8), restarting from best or a pool (9, 11, 22, 28), random radii (10, 14), pair pruning (12), screening (17), swap moves (29), LP repair (34), and other hex-init variants (15, 16, 18, 21, 27, 32). These ranged from +0.0006 to +0.0087.
Next: replicate slot 0 once. Then combine it with slot 6 (analytic gradient and Jacobian) and slot 19 or 33 (L-BFGS-B pre-relaxation). Skip schedule and repair changes. Treat gains under 0.003 as noise.
